definition: A tile is relevant CONUS GIS coverage when at least one 0.05-degree habitat sample-cell center lies inside a U.S. state (cb_2023_us_state_500k, raw) and on terrestrial land (Annual NLCD 2023 land cover present and not class 11 open water).

geometrySource.caveat: Cartographic boundary generalized to 1:500,000; materially finer than the legacy 1:20,000,000 roster geometry and its ~2 km simplification. Shoreline-clipped, so a point inside the polygon is jurisdictional; the NLCD non-water test supplies the terrestrial requirement.
geometrySource.crs: NAD83 (EPSG:4269); reprojected to EPSG:4326 for point tests

landMaskSource.product: Annual NLCD Land Cover, CONUS, 2023, Collection 1 Version 2
landMaskSource.role: Terrestrial mask: a sample cell is land when its NLCD class is present and not 11 (open water).

crossCheckSource.role: Independent full-resolution legal-boundary cross-check of the classification. It agreed on every reclassified tile (zero U.S. land cells for all 23 exclusions, real land cells for all 5 inclusions and every fallback/coastal canary). Not used at runtime.

boundedBuild.authorizedBy: bounded normalization build (finer geometry demonstrated genuine U.S. evidence cells)
boundedBuild.note: One coastal tile (n29_w089, Louisiana delta) exposed an access-state resolution defect: the generalized polygon stopped short of the delta. The runner now unions the normalized land states with the bbox heuristic and the adapter refuses source-less builds; the tile rebuilt with LA as its real source and an honest VERIFIED_EMPTY access layer.

manifestNormalization.retainedR2: Removed assets remain in R2 and the publisher ledger; they are explicit ledger orphans and are never deleted by this tool.
